content: 1. A rapid diagnostic test (RDT) was conducted, and 0% of clients with two consecutive reactive RDT results were confirmed as HIV-positive. A total of 32 discordant cases were identified. 2. Two false-positive results were observed: one case was confirmed as HIV-negative by Western blot despite two reactive RDTs, and the other case involved a client who refused Western blot confirmation. 3. The first assay used was the SD Biostandard Diagnostics test (India). The second assays included the Pareekshak HIV-1/2 Triline card test and the Pareekshak HIV-1/2 rapid test kit (Trispot), both manufactured by Bhat Bio-Tech India Private Limited, Bangalore, Karnataka, India. 4. In a study conducted in Honduras in 1998, involving 3,375 clients, technical errors and unclear testing strategies were reported. Assays used included Retrocell (Abbott Laboratories, USA), Genie 1/2 (Bio-Rad), Multispot (Sanofi Pasteur Diagnostics, France), and HIVCHEK 1+2 (Ortho Diagnostics, France). 5. Specimens tested included HIV-1-positive (n=37), HIV-1-negative (n=1,118), and inconclusive (n=11). Two sera that were positive by Western blot in Honduras and at the CDC were non-reactive in most simple/rapid tests in Honduras but reactive when retested at the CDC. 6. In Rakai, Uganda, in 2007, among 1,517 clients, weak reactive results and poor-quality manufacturer instructions were noted. The serial testing algorithm used included Determine HIV-1/2 (Alere Medical, Japan) as the first assay and HIV-1/2 Stat-Pak (Chembio Diagnostic Systems, USA) as the second assay. 7. In 2012, across three research sites in South Africa and one each in Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia, 9,385 clients were tested. Issues included tie-breaker errors, technical errors, and misinterpretation of results. Parallel testing algorithms were used, with different combinations of Determine HIV-1/2, Uni-Gold HIV, OraQuick Advance HIV-1/2, and Genie II HIV-1/HIV-2. 8. Of 537 participants with positive rapid tests after enrollment, 66 were discordant, and 471 were positive on both rapid tests. 9. In Mozambique in 2013, testing errors and data reporting problems were identified. A serial testing algorithm was used, with Determine HIV-1/2 as the first assay. 10. In Kenya in 2012, 365 individuals providing HIV testing were audited. Issues included failure to adhere to written procedures, transcription errors, poor supervision, and challenges in interpreting test results. 11. In Tanzania in 2012, 100 proficiency testing samples were used to assess 3,835 individuals providing HIV testing across 602 sites. Problems included ineligible providers, incompetent staff, and the use of incorrect RDTs. 12. In Zambia and Rwanda in 2011, 45,820 clients (tested as couples) were evaluated. Cross-reactivity with antibodies from other infections or environmental exposures was noted. Sequential testing with up to three RDTs was performed. 13. In Cambodia in 2005, 563 specimens were tested using Determine HIV-1/2 kits. Technical errors in laboratory reporting were identified. 14. Across 30 countries in Africa in 2012, 16 proficiency testing panels were distributed to 49 laboratories. Challenges included stockouts of test kits, weak reactive results, and poor uptake of external quality assurance (EQA) schemes. 15. In Uganda and Tanzania in 2012, 200 sites were selected for a DTS-based proficiency testing program. Training on DTS reconstitution and HIV testing algorithms was provided, and quarterly feedback was given to ensure corrective measures were applied. 16. In India in 2011, 9,419 specimens were tested using HIV rapid tests. Issues included mislabeling, specimen contamination, and incorrect RDT performance. 17. In Nigeria in 2011, 122 DTS panels were prepared and piloted across 61 sites. Standard operating procedures for rehydration and testing were used. 18. In multiple African countries in 2007, evaluations of commercially available HIV RDTs were conducted. A standardized questionnaire was used to assess test performance, algorithm development, and quality assurance measures. 19. In Lusaka, Zambia, and Kigali, Rwanda, in 2011, 661 clients returned for retesting to resolve their HIV status. False-negative and false-positive results were reported, and some clients continued to receive discordant results. 20. Training sessions for healthcare workers involved in community screening included proper specimen handling, lab safety, and the use of personal protective equipment. Written step-by-step procedures and demonstrations were provided.
